thread:
mia: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal: make precision profiles first-class in the deployment manifest. Keep it declarative, allow runtime negotiation and a minimal safety surface. Thoughts?

sam: +1 to declarative. Two immediate questions:
- should profiles be per-model or per-route?
- do we allow per-request overrides (eg. "prefer_latency")?

jordan: Per-model is safer for caching/kv-compatibility. Per-route makes sense for apps that multiplex models, but mixing precisions across cached KV is scary. We need compatibility checks.

olga: Agreed with jordan. Also we should validate profiles at model-registry publish time. Reject profiles that would break kernel selection or require incompatible KV layout.

mia: Validation + model-registry sounds good. For per-request overrides, maybe allow only "hints" (soft preference) that the runtime can ignore if it would violate SLOs or cache invariants.

arthur: We need explicit runtime contract:
- profile manifest (static)
- negotiation API (runtime decides final precision)
- fallback policy (ordered list, e.g. fp8 -> int8 -> fp16)
- quality floor (metric threshold) to trigger automatic rollback

sam: Design question: where do we store quantization metadata? Options:
1) baked into model artifact (preferred) + lightweight profile in manifest
2) external quant catalog in control plane

jordan: Baking into artifact reduces mismatch risk. But control-plane catalog makes fleet-wide patches easier. Maybe both: canonical metadata in artifact, control-plane can publish overrides with strong audit logs.

olga: Telemetry hooks are critical. We need per-profile counters: token-level latency, top-K perplexity drift, rollout tag. Also sampling for full-eval traces (store prompts + responses for a small percent).

arthur: For rollback automation, suggest these rules:
- monitor a sentinel eval set per-profile
- if quality drops >X% or latency grows >Y% for Z minutes, mark as degraded and failover to next profile
- keep a half-life window to avoid noise

mia: QA bot ran quick smoke on the prototype: 
qa-bot: smoke results: precision=4bit profile on Llama-70B: pass 92/100 prompts within quality threshold, latency 0.8x baseline, fails on long-context math cases; KV-cache misalignment observed in 3/100.

sam: That KV misalignment is the big blocker. Any runtime with mixed precision needs to ensure cache keys include profile id + kernel hash.

jordan: Implementation detail: cache key = hash(model-version + profile-id + sequence-prefix-length + kernel-config). Forces misses on profile switches but avoids corruption.

olga: UX: suggest a canary rollout stage (1% traffic, 10% eval sampling), then 10% traffic, then 100% with automatic health gates.

arthur: Also integrate cost accounting per-profile so sales/finance can map savings to customer bills.

mia: Cool. Action items:
- olga: add profile validation checks to model-registry (ETA: next week)
- jordan: prototype cache-key change + tests (ETA: 2 weeks)
- sam: update deployment manifest RFC with negotiation API (ETA: 1 week)
- arthur: spec telemetry + rollback gates (ETA: 1 week)

mia: Any objections? If not, i'll update the RFC and schedule a quick sync.

sam: no objections :thumbsup:
jordan: lgtm
olga: :+1:
arthur: go for it
